{{one source |date=May 2024}}
In [[physics]] and [[mathematics]], the '''κ-Poincaré algebra''', named after [[Henri Poincaré]], is a deformation of the [[Poincaré algebra]] into a [[Hopf algebra]]. In the [[bicrossproduct]] basis, introduced by Majid-Ruegg<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Majid | first1=S. | last2=Ruegg | first2=H. | title=Bicrossproduct structure of κ-Poincare group and non-commutative geometry | journal=Physics Letters B | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=334 | issue=3–4 | year=1994 | issn=0370-2693 | doi=10.1016/0370-2693(94)90699-8 | pages=348–354|arxiv=hep-th/9405107| bibcode=1994PhLB..334..348M }}</ref> its commutation rules reads:

* <math>[P_\mu, P_\nu] = 0 </math>
* <math> [R_j , P_0] = 0, \; [R_j , P_k] = i \varepsilon_{jkl} P_l, \; [R_j , N_k] = i \varepsilon_{jkl} N_l, \; [R_j , R_k] = i \varepsilon_{jkl} R_l</math>
* <math>[N_j , P_0] = i P_j, \;[N_j , P_k] = i \delta_{jk} \left(  \frac{1 - e^{- 2 \lambda P_0}}{2 \lambda}  + \frac{ \lambda }{2}  |\vec{P}|^2 \right) - i \lambda P_j P_k, \; [N_j,N_k] = -i \varepsilon_{jkl} R_l</math>

Where <math>P_\mu</math> are the translation generators, <math>R_j</math> the rotations and <math>N_j</math> the boosts.
The [[coproducts]] are:
* <math>\Delta P_j =  P_j \otimes 1 +  e^{- \lambda P_0} \otimes P_j ~, \qquad \Delta P_0  = P_0 \otimes 1 + 1 \otimes P_0</math>
* <math>\Delta R_j  = R_j \otimes 1 +  1 \otimes R_j</math>
* <math>\Delta N_k  =  N_k \otimes 1 + e^{-\lambda P_0} \otimes N_k  + i \lambda \varepsilon_{klm}  P_l \otimes R_m .</math>

The [[Hopf algebra|antipodes]] and the [[Hopf algebra|counits]]:
* <math>S(P_0) =  - P_0</math>
* <math>S(P_j) =  -e^{\lambda P_0} P_j</math>
* <math>S(R_j) =  - R_j</math>
* <math>S(N_j)  =  -e^{\lambda P_0}N_j +i \lambda \varepsilon_{jkl} e^{\lambda P_0} P_k R_l</math>
* <math>\varepsilon(P_0) =  0</math>
* <math>\varepsilon(P_j) =  0</math>
* <math>\varepsilon(R_j) =  0</math>
* <math>\varepsilon(N_j)  = 0</math>

The κ-Poincaré algebra is the dual Hopf algebra to the [[κ-Poincaré group]], and can be interpreted as its “infinitesimal” version.
